keywords.def: meal from a supermarket that has already been prepared and can be heated up and eaten later
(idiom) from the very beginning, without using anything that has already been made
something you enjoy but feel embarrassed about, or think you should not do
(idiom) saying advising that it’s best to avoid too much of anything

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这是BBC学英语的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Pippa. If you've eaten anything today, then it's likely that some of your food was ultra-processed – food containing artificial ingredients like additives and sweeteners.
sentences.zh: 我是Phil。我是Pippa。如果你今天吃过东西，那么你吃的一些食物很可能是超加工食品——含有添加剂和甜味剂等人工成分的食物。

sentences.en: Ultra-processed foods are everywhere, from sliced bread to chocolate biscuits and crisps.
sentences.zh: 超加工食品无处不在，从切片面包到巧克力饼干和薯片。

sentences.en: They might taste good, but the bad news is that ultra-processed foods have been linked to poor health.
sentences.zh: 它们可能尝起来不错，但坏消息是超加工食品与健康状况不佳有关。

sentences.en: They often contain lots of sugar and salt and have been linked to problems like obesity and diabetes.
sentences.zh: 它们通常含有大量的糖和盐，并与肥胖和糖尿病等问题有关。

sentences.en: So, how can we tell what food is ultra-processed and what's not?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们如何分辨哪些食物是超加工食品，哪些不是呢？

sentences.en: Here's health reporter Annabel Rackham on BBC World Service programme What in the World?
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC世界频道节目What in the World的健康记者Annabel Rackham。

sentences.en: Ultra-processed foods are things that contain five or more ingredients, and things that you wouldn't find in your average kitchen.
sentences.zh: 超加工食品是含有五种或更多成分的食物，以及你在普通厨房里找不到的东西。

sentences.en: It's going to have things on there, like emulsifiers, preservatives, additives, dyes and sweeteners.
sentences.zh: 它里面会有些东西，比如乳化剂、防腐剂、添加剂、色素和甜味剂。

sentences.en: Annabel describes ultra-processed foods as things containing ingredients you wouldn't find in your kitchen.
sentences.zh: Annabel将超加工食品描述为包含你在厨房里找不到的成分的东西。

sentences.en: Do you eat much ultra-processed food, Pippa, or do you try to avoid it?
sentences.zh: Pippa，你吃很多超加工食品吗，还是尽量避开它们？

sentences.en: I used to eat a lot of ultra-processed foods, and now I try to cook everything myself and not eat things like chocolate and snacks all day.
sentences.zh: 我以前吃很多超加工食品，现在我尽量自己做饭，不整天吃巧克力和零食之类的东西。

sentences.en: How about you? I think the same. I try to cook things using just normal ingredients, just so you know what's gone into it.
sentences.zh: 你呢？我想也一样。我尽量用普通食材做饭，这样你才知道里面加了什么。

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll be discussing ultra-processed food as well as learning some useful new vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将讨论超加工食品，并学习一些有用的新词汇。

sentences.en: And remember, there's also a quiz and worksheet available on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 记住，我们的网站bbclearningenglish.com上也提供有测验和练习单。

sentences.en: But now I have a question for you, Pippa.
sentences.zh: 但现在我有一个问题要问你，Pippa。

sentences.en: Fizzy drinks, like cola and lemonade, are another example of popular ultra-processed foods, but when were fizzy drinks invented?
sentences.zh: 碳酸饮料，比如可乐和柠檬水，是另一种受欢迎的超加工食品的例子，但是碳酸饮料是什么时候发明的？

sentences.en: Was it: a) 1772, b) 1872, or c) 1972? Well, I think it was before 1972, but 1772 sounds like too early, so I'm going to say b) 1872.
sentences.zh: 是：a) 1772年，b) 1872年，还是 c) 1972年？嗯，我认为是在1972年之前，但1772年听起来太早了，所以我要选 b) 1872年。

sentences.en: We'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 我们将在节目结束时揭晓答案。

sentences.en: One reason for the popularity of ultra-processed food is convenience.
sentences.zh: 超加工食品受欢迎的一个原因就是方便。

sentences.en: Let's hear more from health reporter Annabel, who talks here with Hannah Gelbart, presenter of BBC World Service's What in the World.
sentences.zh: 让我们听听健康记者Annabel的更多介绍，她在这里与BBC世界频道What in the World的主持人Hannah Gelbart进行了交谈。

sentences.en: So, I do think convenience – it is the main issue there.
sentences.zh: 所以，我确实认为方便——这是主要问题。

sentences.en: And again, with a ready meal, you put it in the microwave for a couple of minutes.
sentences.zh: 还有，买一份预制菜，你把它放进微波炉几分钟。

sentences.en: It's done. It's hot. It serves you. Whereas, you know, sometimes cooking a fresh meal from scratch – that can take a really long time.
sentences.zh: 就好了。热的。端给你。然而，你知道，有时从头开始做一顿新鲜的饭菜——那可能需要很长时间。

sentences.en: What's your ultra-processed guilty food?
sentences.zh: 你最内疚的超加工食品是什么？

sentences.en: I'm a chocolate girl. A packet of biscuits – something like that.
sentences.zh: 我是个巧克力女孩。一包饼干——诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: A cake. That is my... that's my guilty pleasure.
sentences.zh: 一块蛋糕。那是我的……那是我的罪恶享受。

sentences.en: Ultra-processed foods like ready meals are convenient.
sentences.zh: 像预制菜这样的超加工食品很方便。

sentences.en: A ready meal is a meal from a supermarket that has already been prepared and can be heated up quickly in a microwave.
sentences.zh: 预制菜是指超市里已经准备好、可以在微波炉里快速加热的饭菜。

sentences.en: That's a lot quicker and easier than cooking from scratch – an idiom meaning to do something from the very beginning without using anything that's already been made.
sentences.zh: 这比从头开始做饭要快得多、容易得多——这是一个习语，指从头开始做某事，不使用任何已经做好的东西。

sentences.en: Even though ultra-processed foods are often unhealthy, they taste good.
sentences.zh: 尽管超加工食品通常不健康，但它们尝起来很好吃。

sentences.en: That's why Annabel calls chocolate her guilty pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么Annabel称巧克力为她的罪恶享受。

sentences.en: A guilty pleasure is something you enjoy but think you shouldn't and feel a little embarrassed about.
sentences.zh: 罪恶享受是指你喜欢但认为不应该喜欢并为此感到有点尴尬的事情。

sentences.en: Ultra-processed food is a tricky topic. We know these foods have been linked to poor health, but at the same time they're cheap, convenient and taste good.
sentences.zh: 超加工食品是一个棘手的话题。我们知道这些食物与健康状况不佳有关，但同时它们又便宜、方便而且好吃。

sentences.en: So, what should we do? Here's Hannah and Annabel discussing this for BBC programme What in the World: Is it OK for me to have a packet of crisps once in a while?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们该怎么办？这里是Hannah和Annabel在BBC节目What in the World中讨论这个问题：我偶尔吃一包薯片可以吗？

sentences.en: Should we be cutting ultra-processed foods out of our diets completely, or is there a way for us to still enjoy them from time to time?
sentences.zh: 我们应该把超加工食品完全从我们的饮食中剔除，还是有一种方法让我们偶尔还能享受它们？

sentences.en: I think the best thing to do is just not to panic.
sentences.zh: 我认为最好的做法是不要惊慌。

sentences.en: Everything is fine in moderation. Hannah asks if it's OK to eat ultra-processed foods once in a while, or from time to time.
sentences.zh: 凡事适度就好。Hannah询问偶尔吃一次超加工食品，或者不时吃一次是否可以。

sentences.en: The phrases once in a while and from time to time mean occasionally – sometimes, but not very often.
sentences.zh: 短语once in a while和from time to time的意思是偶尔——有时，但不经常。

sentences.en: Annabel replies using the phrase everything in moderation, which advises us that it's best to avoid too much of anything.
sentences.zh: Annabel用everything in moderation这个短语回应，建议我们最好避免任何东西过量。

sentences.en: That sounds sensible to me, and it also means I won't feel bad about eating chocolate now and then.
sentences.zh: 这听这也挺合理的，这也意味着我偶尔吃巧克力也不会感到内疚。

sentences.en: OK. Pippa, it's time to reveal the answer to my question.
sentences.zh: 好的。Pippa，是时候揭晓我的问题答案了。

sentences.en: Now, I asked you when fizzy drinks were invented.
sentences.zh: 现在，我问你碳酸饮料是什么时候发明的。

sentences.en: You said 1872. I'm afraid the correct answer was 1772.
sentences.zh: 你说是1872年。恐怕正确答案是1772年。

sentences.en: Apparently carbonated water was used to try to prevent scurvy on sea voyages.
sentences.zh: 显然，当时人们试图用碳酸水来预防海上航行的坏血病。

sentences.en: Wow, that is amazing. I wouldn't have thought it was that long ago.
sentences.zh: 哇，太惊人了。我不会想到那是那么久以前的事了。

sentences.en: Right. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with ready meal – a meal from a supermarket that has already been prepared so you can heat it up quickly.
sentences.zh: 对。让我们回顾一下我们学过的词汇，从ready meal开始——这是一种来自超市的已经准备好的饭菜，你可以快速加热。

sentences.en: If you do something from scratch, you do it from the very beginning, without using anything that's already been made.
sentences.zh: 如果你from scratch做某事，你就是从最开始做，不使用任何已经做好的东西。

sentences.en: A guilty pleasure is something you enjoy but feel guilty or embarrassed about because you think you shouldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 罪恶享受是指你喜欢但又感到内疚或尴尬的事情，因为你认为你不应该这样做。

sentences.en: The phrases once in a while and from time to time mean occasionally, not very often.
sentences.zh: 短语once in a while和from time to time的意思是偶尔，不经常。

sentences.en: And finally, the phrase everything in moderation is used to advise someone that it's best to avoid too much of anything.
sentences.zh: 最后，短语everything in moderation用于建议某人最好避免任何东西过量。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you're hungry for more, head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, for more tasty topics and useful vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了，但如果你还想了解更多，请访问我们的网站bbclearningenglish.com，获取更多有趣的话题和有用的词汇。

sentences.en: See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 很快再见。但现在，我们要说再见了。

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
